newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent lower Friday, in line with losses in London overnight, traders said.
LIFFE robusta futures sagged in thin, rangebound trade. At the midday break, September was down $20 at $1,621 a tonne, traded $1,630 to $1,620. November fell the same to $1,611.
Thursday, New York arabica futures ended mixed, with much of the activity focused on the nearby switches and options ahead of September options expiry today.

September settled down 1.25 cents at 184.50 cents a lb after ranging from 191.50 to 181.50 cents. Second-month December rose 1.20 cents to 162.55 cents, tightening the September/December switch to 21.95 cents compared with 24.40 cents at the close on Wednesday.
The back months closed down 1.25 to 2.80 cents.
Traders expected September options expiry to have little impact on today's trading. "It's already in the market," said one dealer.
Technically, traders pegged September support at 181.50-180.00 cents, followed by 178.00 cents. On the upside, they said resistance was seen near 190.00 cents.
After Thursday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 250 60-kg bags as of July 30, to 92,399 bags. An additional 750 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday that mild weather is expected through the first half of next week in Brazil's coffee belt, with somewhat cooler temperatures possible during the second half of the week..
WSC said, however, a high pressure expected to build in Argentina next week is forecast to pass well to the south of coffee growing areas.
